example.name: complete_retail_model
example.scenario: Create a complete retail analytics semantic model with fact table (store_sales), dimension tables (date_dim, customers, products), relationships, and metrics. Based on the TPC-DS benchmark model from the OSI repository.
example.user_request: Create an OSI semantic model for retail sales analytics with customer, product, and date dimensions. Include revenue and profit metrics.

step.description: Identify source tables and business domain
step.approach: Review the source database schema to identify fact and dimension tables. Confirm column names, data types, and existing relationships. Outcome: list of tables with their columns and keys.
step.expected_outcome: Fact: store_sales. Dimensions: date_dim, customers, products, stores

step.approach: Create dataset entries with source references in database.schema.table format. Add primary keys, unique keys, and ai_context synonyms. Outcome: dataset definitions for all fact and dimension tables.
step.analysis: Each dataset needs name, source, and at least one key definition.

step.approach: For each dataset, create field entries with ANSI_SQL expressions. Mark time dimensions with is_time: true. Add descriptions and ai_context synonyms. Outcome: complete field definitions for all datasets.
Create relationship entries linking store_sales to each dimension. Specify from (store_sales), to (dimension), and matching columns. Outcome: relationship definitions for all fact-dimension joins.
Create metric entries for total_revenue, total_profit, avg_order_value. Use qualified expressions referencing dataset.field paths. Outcome: metric definitions with descriptions and synonyms.

artifact.osi_model:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../core-spec/osi-schema.json version: "0.1.1"
semantic_model: - name: retail_sales_analytics description: Retail sales analytics model with customer, product, and date dimensions ai_context: instructions: "Use this model for retail sales analysis, customer insights, and product performance metrics." synonyms: ["sales", "retail", "revenue", "profit"]
datasets: - name: store_sales source: analytics.public.store_sales primary_key: [ss_item_sk, ss_ticket_number] description: Fact table containing all store sales transactions ai_context: synonyms: ["sales transactions", "store purchases"] fields: - name: ss_sold_date_sk expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: ss_sold_date_sk description: Foreign key to date dimension - name: ss_customer_sk expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: ss_customer_sk description: Foreign key to customer dimension - name: ss_item_sk expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: ss_item_sk description: Foreign key to product dimension - name: ss_quantity expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: ss_quantity description: Quantity of items sold - name: ss_sales_price expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: ss_sales_price description: Sales price per unit - name: ss_net_profit expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: ss_net_profit description: Net profit from the sale
- name: date_dim source: analytics.public.date_dim primary_key: [d_date_sk] description: Date dimension with calendar attributes fields: - name: d_date_sk expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: d_date_sk - name: d_date expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: d_date dimension: is_time: true - name: d_year expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: d_year dimension: is_time: true - name: d_month_name expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: d_month_name dimension: is_time: true
- name: customers source: analytics.public.customers primary_key: [c_customer_sk] description: Customer dimension table fields: - name: c_customer_sk expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: c_customer_sk - name: c_customer_name expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: c_customer_name ai_context: synonyms: ["customer name", "buyer name"]
- name: products source: analytics.public.products primary_key: [p_item_sk] description: Product dimension table fields: - name: p_item_sk expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: p_item_sk - name: p_product_name expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: p_product_name ai_context: synonyms: ["product name", "item name"]
relationships: - name: store_sales_to_date from: store_sales to: date_dim from_columns: [ss_sold_date_sk] to_columns: [d_date_sk] - name: store_sales_to_customers from: store_sales to: customers from_columns: [ss_customer_sk] to_columns: [c_customer_sk] - name: store_sales_to_products from: store_sales to: products from_columns: [ss_item_sk] to_columns: [p_item_sk]
metrics: - name: total_revenue expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: SUM(store_sales.ss_quantity * store_sales.ss_sales_price) description: Total revenue from all sales ai_context: synonyms: ["total sales", "gross revenue"] - name: total_profit expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: SUM(store_sales.ss_net_profit) description: Total net profit from all sales - name: avg_order_value expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: SUM(store_sales.ss_sales_price * store_sales.ss_quantity) / COUNT(DISTINCT store_sales.ss_ticket_number) description: Average revenue per order

example.completion: The retail_sales_analytics model includes 1 fact table (store_sales), 3 dimension tables (date_dim, customers, products), 3 relationships, and 3 metrics. All fields have ANSI_SQL expressions, time dimensions are marked, and ai_context includes synonyms for LLM discovery.

key_takeaways.takeaway: Use database.schema.table format for source references
Mark all time dimension fields with is_time: true
Include ai_context synonyms for better LLM query generation
Relationship from_columns must match the fact table foreign keys

example.name: dbt_integration_model
example.scenario: Create an OSI model with DBT vendor extensions for a marketing analytics domain.
example.user_request: Build an OSI semantic model for marketing campaigns with DBT integration metadata.

step.approach: Create campaigns (fact) and channels (dimension) datasets. Add DBT custom_extensions with materialized and tags configuration. Outcome: datasets with vendor-specific metadata.

example.artifact:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../core-spec/osi-schema.json version: "0.1.1"
semantic_model: - name: marketing_analytics description: Marketing campaign performance model datasets: - name: campaigns source: marketing.public.campaigns primary_key: [campaign_id] custom_extensions: - vendor_name: DBT data: '{"project_name": "marketing_analytics", "materialized": "table", "tags": ["daily"]}' fields: - name: campaign_id expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: campaign_id - name: spend expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: spend description: Campaign spend amount - name: channels source: marketing.public.channels primary_key: [channel_id] custom_extensions: - vendor_name: DBT data: '{"project_name": "marketing_analytics", "materialized": "dimension"}' fields: - name: channel_id expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: channel_id - name: channel_name expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: channel_name ai_context: synonyms: ["marketing channel", "ad channel"] relationships: - name: campaigns_to_channels from: campaigns to: channels from_columns: [channel_id] to_columns: [channel_id] metrics: - name: total_spend expression: dialects: - dialect: ANSI_SQL expression: SUM(campaigns.spend) description: Total marketing spend

key_takeaways.takeaway: DBT extensions carry materialized type and tags for pipeline integration
Vendor extensions use JSON strings within the data field
